headline: Uproar in parliament as MP Rumeen Farhana criticises BNP over corruption
summary: Independent MP Rumeen Farhana's remarks on energy crises and corruption during the BNP's tenure sparked intense protests and chaos in the National Parliament.
details: Independent MP Rumeen Farhana sparked an uproar in the National Parliament today during discussions on the Bank Resolution (Amendment) Bill 2026.

Farhana claimed that if the BNP comes to power, it is 'impossible' for there to be no gas, electricity, or fertiliser crises, and that Bangladesh would likely top the list of corruption and loan defaults.
Her remarks triggered loud protests from BNP MPs, leading to a chaotic scene where opposition lawmakers alleged that ruling party members hurled 'objectionable remarks' at her.
Rumeen Farhana compared the intolerance in parliament to the 'Awami League era,' stating that the BNP is now behaving even worse than the previous regime.
Deputy Speaker Kayser Kamal repeatedly tried to restore order, reminding lawmakers that every MP has the right to speak and that disruption is contrary to democratic norms.
Opposition Leader Shafiqur Rahman questioned whether Rumeen's rights as an MP were being upheld, as her speech was drowned out by the chaos.
The session ended with the ruling party supporting the Bank Resolution (Amendment) Bill 2026, while the opposition remained silent during the vote.
Rumeen Farhana left the chamber during the passage of the bill.
caption:

Independent MP Rumeen Farhana sparked an uproar in the National Parliament today during discussions on the Bank Resolution (Amendment) Bill 2026.

Farhana claimed that if the BNP comes to power, it is 'impossible' for there to be no gas, electricity, or fertiliser crises, and that Bangladesh would likely top the list of corruption and loan defaults.

Her remarks triggered loud protests from BNP MPs, leading to a chaotic scene where opposition lawmakers alleged that ruling party members hurled 'objectionable remarks' at her.

Rumeen Farhana compared the intolerance in parliament to the 'Awami League era,' stating that the BNP is now behaving even worse than the previous regime.

Deputy Speaker Kayser Kamal repeatedly tried to restore order, reminding lawmakers that every MP has the right to speak and that disruption is contrary to democratic norms.

Opposition Leader Shafiqur Rahman questioned whether Rumeen's rights as an MP were being upheld, as her speech was drowned out by the chaos.

The session ended with the ruling party supporting the Bank Resolution (Amendment) Bill 2026, while the opposition remained silent during the vote.

Rumeen Farhana left the chamber during the passage of the bill.

headline: Over 1,000 children dead from measles and suspected cases in Bangladesh
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reports a record-breaking death toll, marking a catastrophic surge in a preventable disease.
details: The death toll from measles and suspected cases has surpassed 1,000 children in Bangladesh, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS). This marks the highest number of deaths from the disease in the country's history.
caption:
Over 1,000 children have died from measles and suspected cases—the highest death toll in Bangladesh's history.
